# msgpunsafe — Usage Context

## What this is

`msgpunsafe` (`github.com/sirkon/msgpunsafe`) is a zero-dependency Go library of
**unsafe, panic-based deserialization primitives for msgpack (MessagePack)**.
It is a library only: no executable, no CLI, no `main` package. It is designed
to back generated msgpack decoders (the `ErrorStruct*` /
`ErrorRequiredFieldMissing` codes exist for that purpose; the generated-code
consumer lives in another repo).

Every consumer-facing function is named `Take*` and reads exactly one value
from a raw byte buffer using a `src`/`lim` pointer-pair cursor model. Failures
are reported by **panicking with an `ErrorCode`** (never a returned error).

## Cursor model (core concept)

A decode position is a pair of `unsafe.Pointer`s:

- `src` — current read position.
- `lim` — one-past-the-end bound of the whole buffer.

Every `Take*` returns `(value, nextPtr)` where `nextPtr` is the advanced cursor;
the caller is responsible for threading `nextPtr` into the next call. Bounds
checks compare `uintptr(src)` against `uintptr(lim)` *before* dereferencing;
multi-byte reads additionally verify `uintptr(lim)-uintptr(src) >= size+1`.

## Quick usage example

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "unsafe"

    "github.com/sirkon/msgpunsafe"
)

func decode(input []byte) (err error) {
    defer msgpunsafe.HandleError(recover(), &err)

    // Build the cursor pair.
    src := unsafe.Pointer(&input[0])
    lim := unsafe.Add(src, len(input))

    // Reusable arena so returned strings/pointers outlive the temp buffer.
    buf := msgpunsafe.NewSafeBuffer(512)

    n, src := msgpunsafe.TakeInt64(src, lim)       // a number
    s, src := msgpunsafe.TakeString(src, lim, buf) // a string (copied)
    b, src := msgpunsafe.TakeBool(src, lim)        // a bool
    _ = b

    fmt.Println(n, s)
    return nil
}
```

Note: `HandleError` must be the first thing in a `defer` so it wraps the
`recover()` call. It converts a valid `ErrorCode` panic into `*err` and
re-panics anything else.

## API reference

### Headers (`headers.go`)

| Function | Signature | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `TakeSliceHeader` | `(src, lim)` | `(elementCount, next)` for array markers `0x90-0x9f`, `0xdc`, `0xdd` |
| `TakeMapHeader` | `(src, lim)` | `(pairCount, next)` for map markers `0x80-0x8f`, `0xde`, `0xdf` |
| `TakeStrHeader` | `(src, lim)` | `(byteSize, dataPtr)` for str markers `0xa0-0xbf`, `0xd9-0xdb` |
| `TakeBinHeader` | `(src, lim)` | `(byteSize, dataPtr)` for bin markers `0xc4-0xc6` |

### Scalars

| Function | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `TakeUint`, `TakeUint8/16/32/64` | `(uintN, next)` | overflow panics if value doesn't fit |
| `TakeInt`, `TakeInt8/16/32/64` | `(intN, next)` | overflow panics if value doesn't fit |
| `TakeFloat32`, `TakeFloat64` | `(floatN, next)` | |
| `TakeBool` | `(bool, next)` | markers `0xc2`/`0xc3` |
| `IsNil` | `(bool, ptr)` | `0xc0`; **pointer unchanged when non-nil** (exception to the next-pointer rule) |

### Strings and bytes (`string_and_bytes.go`)

| Function | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `TakeString` | `(string, next)` | copies into `*SafeBuffer`; survives temp buffer reuse |
| `TakeStringZC` | `(string, next)` | zero-copy; points **into** caller's buffer, caller must keep it alive |
| `TakeBytes` | `([]byte, next)` | copies into `*SafeBuffer` |

### Pointer-returning variants (`numbers_ptr.go`, `bool.go`)

`TakeIntPtr`, `TakeInt8Ptr` … `TakeUintPtr` … `TakeFloat32Ptr`/`TakeFloat64Ptr`
and `TakeBoolPtr` parse via the scalar `Take*`, store the value in an
8-byte-aligned `SafeBuffer` slot (`AllocAligned`), and return `(*T, next)`.
Used where the generated decoder needs a stable pointer to a field.

### Skip (`skip.go`)

`TakeSkip(src, lim) unsafe.Pointer` skips one complete msgpack object
(containers recursively) using an explicit stack, with **zero allocation**.
It returns the pointer just past the object. Own error family
(`ErrorSkip*`), recursion limit `skipRecursionLimit = 100000`.

### SafeBuffer (`safebuf.go`)

`NewSafeBuffer(cap)` preallocates a reusable arena. Prefer `cap <= 512` and
reuse the buffer across decodes.

> **Default buffer size = fastest (benchmarked).** Sweeping `SafeBuffer`
> capacity over a realistic string-decode workload (`BenchmarkTakeString_*` in
> `bench_test.go`), the 512-byte default is the throughput sweet spot:
>
> | capacity | `NewSafeBuffer` cost | fresh-buffer decode | reused-buffer decode |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 64 B | 14 ns / 64 B / 1 alloc | ~178 ns | ~178 ns |
> | 128 B | 20 ns / 128 B / 1 alloc | ~131 ns | ~130 ns |
> | 256 B | 32 ns / 256 B / 1 alloc | ~115 ns / 2 allocs | ~106 ns / 1 alloc |
> | **512 B** | **60 ns** / 512 B / 1 alloc | **~115 ns / 1 alloc** | **~109 ns / 0 allocs** |
> | 1024 B | 110 ns / 1024 B / 1 alloc | ~171 ns | ~96 ns / 0 allocs |
> | 2048 B | 220 ns / 2048 B / 1 alloc | ~291 ns | ~93 ns / 0 allocs |
> | 4096 B | 430 ns / 4096 B / 1 alloc | ~495 ns | ~96 ns / 0 allocs |
>
> 512 is the best *combined* choice: it is large enough that a message's
> strings fit without a mid-decode reset (0 extra allocs when reused), yet small
> enough that allocating/zeroing the arena stays cheap. Larger capacities only
> shave ~10 ns off the reused-buffer steady state while costing up to 7× more
> upfront allocation; smaller capacities pay more in extra clone/alloc calls.

- `AllocString(data, size) string` / `AllocBytes(data, size) []byte` — copy into
  the arena so the result outlives the temporary source (e.g. a Tarantool
  response buffer). If `size > cap` they fall back to a direct
  `strings.Clone`/`bytes.Clone`; otherwise they reset/append into the backing
  array (previously returned headers keep prior backing arrays alive).
- `AllocAligned(size) unsafe.Pointer` — reserves a slot aligned to
  `ptrAlignment = 8`; the caller must write the full value immediately. Its
  direct-fallback threshold is `size+7 > cap` (not `size > cap`), so a reset
  buffer can never loop forever.

### Error handling (`errors.go`)

- `HandleError(r any, err *error)` — recover helper for `defer`: maps a valid
  `ErrorCode` panic to `*err`, re-panics anything else.
- `ErrorCode` is an `int` implementing `error`. `Error()` and `IsValid()` panic
  on out-of-range codes (this is how `HandleError` distinguishes msgs errors
  from unrelated panics).
- Error categories per type: `*Exhausted`, `*HeaderTruncated`,
  `*HeaderCorrupted`, `*LenConflict`, `*Overflow`, `*Corrupted`.

## Commands

```sh
go test ./...                          # default build (non-aligned readout)
go test -tags=aware_of_alignment ./... # alignment-safe readout
go vet ./...
go vet -tags=aware_of_alignment ./...
```

- Go 1.26 (see `go.mod`); relies on Go 1.22+ (`for range N`) and Go 1.25
  (`sync.Go` in tests).
- No CI, no Makefile, no linter config. `go test` is the only gate.
- **Gotcha:** `go test -race ./...` crashes with
  `fatal error: checkptr: pointer arithmetic result points to invalid allocation`
  in `ptrs()` (`testhelp_test.go`), where `unsafe.Add(p, len(input))` computes
  `lim` past the slice's real allocation. Test-helper limitation only; plain and
  `-tags=aware_of_alignment` runs pass.

## Architecture

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `headers.go` | Container/str/bin header readers. |
| `numbers.go` | Typed wrappers `TakeUint*`/`TakeInt*`/`TakeFloat*` that call internal `take*` and narrow with overflow `panic`. |
| `numbers_base.go` | Numeric decoding, **`//go:build !aware_of_alignment` (default)** — native-endian cast + `bits.ReverseBytes*`. Fast, unsafe on unaligned buffers. |
| `numbers_base_align.go` | Numeric decoding, **`//go:build aware_of_alignment`** — `encoding/binary.BigEndian` over `unsafe.Slice`. Alignment-safe, slower. Keep in lockstep with `numbers_base.go`. |
| `bool.go` | `TakeBool`, `TakeBoolPtr`. |
| `nil.go` | `IsNil`. |
| `string_and_bytes.go` | `TakeString`, `TakeStringZC`, `TakeBytes`. |
| `safebuf.go` | `SafeBuffer` arena. |
| `numbers_ptr.go` | `Take*Ptr` variants for int/uint/float widths. |
| `skip.go` | `TakeSkip` and its `ErrorSkip*` family. |
| `errors.go` | `ErrorCode`, messages, `HandleError`, `panicWithError`. |

## Non-obvious behavior

- **Cross-signedness parsing:** `takeUint64` also parses `0xd0-0xd3` (int
  markers) as unsigned, panicking `ErrorUintOverflow` on negatives; `takeInt64`
  also parses `0xcc-0xcf` (uint markers), panicking `ErrorIntOverflow` above
  `math.MaxInt64`. Deliberate, for compatibility.
- **`IsNil` return convention:** unchanged `src` on non-nil (all other `Take*`
  return the advanced pointer).
- **Wrong-type header markers** are reported only as `*HeaderCorrupted` (open
  TODO in `headers.go` about distinguishing e.g. map-vs-array).
- **Two numeric backends:** when changing numeric decoding, edit BOTH
  `numbers_base.go` and `numbers_base_align.go` and test with both build tags.

## Conventions

- Public API `Take*` with full godoc comments (godoc is the only documentation;
  `README.md` is a stub). Internal helpers are lowercase (`take*`,
  `panicWithError`).
- Errors are panics with `ErrorCode`, recovered via `HandleError`.
- Multi-byte reads bounds-check `uintptr(lim)-uintptr(src)` against total bytes
  needed (lead byte + payload).
- Adding an `ErrorCode`: append at the **end** of the const block and extend
  `errorMessages` in matching index order. `ErrorSliceExhausted` is `iota == 0`;
  tests use `wantErrCode == 0` as "no panic expected", so never introduce a new
  zero code.

## Testing

- One `_test.go` per source file plus `testhelp_test.go` (shared helpers).
- `testhelp_test.go`: `b(...byte)` builds payloads; `ptrs(input)` builds the
  `(src, lim)` pair (empty input → two equal pointers = "exhausted");
  `runTake[T](...)` runs any `Take*` under `recover` and asserts either the exact
  `ErrorCode` or full-buffer consumption. Reuse these; don't duplicate.
- Table-driven per typed wrapper, each covering happy path (all encodings),
  truncation, corruption, exhaustion, and narrowing overflow. `numbers_test.go`
  is the model to copy.
- `safebuf_test.go` asserts returned pointers physically live inside/outside the
  backing array (`ptrInBuf`) and hammers `runtime.GC()` for retention.
- gopls warns that `numbers_base_align.go` is excluded by build tags (expected);
  add `-tags=aware_of_alignment` to gopls build flags if you edit it often.
